title: POC Integration & Connectivity Sprint Sync
summary: Weekly sync focusing on networking interop, kernel/MTU upgrade impacts, routing fallbacks, and next-step benchmarks for Redwood Private pilot. Action items assigned for benchmarking, canary rollout plan, and security paperwork follow-up.
topics: MTU and kernel upgrade impact analysis
next_steps: Redwood to share canary rollout playbook and proposed schedule
Asteron to provide latest network topology + peering configs by 2027-04-16
Marcus to run 95th-pct latency and tail-burn benchmark and share results by 2027-04-21
Security to review KMS/KPIs doc and revert with questions by 2027-04-20
action_items: Marcus Rivera - run e2e throughput and 95th percentile tail latency benchmarks (batch sizes 1,4,8) - due 2027-04-21
Priya Desai - export VPC routing tables and peering configs for staging and prod - due 2027-04-16
Olivia Chen - send canary rollout playbook + fallback thresholds doc - due 2027-04-15

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-04-14
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Rivera (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM); Priya Desai (Asteron Platform), Tomás Alvarez (Asteron NetOps), Eve Marshall (Asteron CTO), Benji Rao (Asteron Security)

Summary (auto): Quick check-in on pilot progress; main blockers around MTU/kernel mismatch causing packet fragmentation on egress, a flaky peering route in one AZ, and a question on telemetry spans making it into Asteron's datadog. Agreed on steps to run bench-marking, share configs, and stage a small canary.

Transcript:
00:00 Olivia Chen: okay everyone uh let's get started, thanks for making time. um short agenda - networking updates, kernel/MTU work, fallback behavior, telemetry, and then next steps. sound good?
00:09 Priya Desai: yep that works. sorry small background noise, we're on a sprint window so hope to be concise.
00:15 Marcus Rivera: quick note - we validated the KV cache hit-rate change from last week; small improvement but not the main cause of the tail. filing that as low priority for this sync.
00:28 Tomás Alvarez: right the big thing for us is egress fragmentation. after your kernel bump to 5.15 we saw MTU mismatch on the tunnel and some packets get dropped between our edge and the private cluster.
00:40 Olivia Chen: okay can you say more about which tunnel? is this the transit VPC peering or the direct interconnect?
00:46 Tomás Alvarez: it's the transit peering to us-east-2, specifically the b-az subnet. looks like PMTU discovery isn't working reliably across the jump. sometimes we fall back to pmtu blackhole behavior.
00:58 Marcus Rivera: hmm that aligns with the metrics — we saw retransmits during bursts. two quick thoughts: 1) we can force path MTU on the egress and pin the MSS on the TCP flow from the gateway; 2) if we do the kernel rollback to older netstack configs it may change latency. both have tradeoffs.
01:18 Priya Desai: tradeoffs meaning more CPU or higher latency?
01:21 Marcus Rivera: yes CPU on the gateway if we do MSS clamping, and if we rollback kernel you might see slightly different networking stacks which could impact throughput characteristic under high concurrency.
01:31 Eve Marshall: my concern is production parity - we don't want an approach that makes staging look great but production mismatches. can we get an isolated canary?
01:38 Olivia Chen: absolutely — canary is what we recommend. small percentage of traffic to a set of hosts with the kernel patch and with our fallback - circuit breaker - enabled. that way we can validate both the MTU fix and the graceful degradation paths.
01:50 Benji Rao: security question - if we change the MTU or do MSS clamp, do we need to update any firewall rules or DPI?
01:55 Tomás Alvarez: maybe, some of our middleboxes expect specific fragment behavior.
01:59 Marcus Rivera: good call; we'll need the topology. Priya can you share the middlebox list and peering ACLs?
02:05 Priya Desai: yes I can export those. I'll put them in the shared folder - apologies it's a bit messy but I'll attach notes.
02:11 Olivia Chen: thanks. on fallback behavior - last week we instrumented a routing fallback rule so requests that cross a latency threshold route to a lower-cost model variant hosted locally in your VPC. We noticed it tripped unexpectedly during a small burst. Marcus, any insight?
02:24 Marcus Rivera: yeah the threshold evaluation window was 30s and it was sensitive to a quick spike; the circuit-breaker closed then reopened but there was a small flapping. we've proposed smoothing the window to 90s and adding a minimum request count before triggering.
02:36 Tomás Alvarez: that seems reasonable. what about cache warmup for that variant - if we reroute, cold KV cache would blow latency out.
02:43 Marcus Rivera: correct which is why our canary plan includes pre-warming the KV cache with representative prefixes. we'll push a preload script.
02:51 Eve Marshall: can you show the script or a snippet so our ops team can review?
02:55 Marcus Rivera: yes I can paste a gist to the shared folder after the call.
03:00 Olivia Chen: telemetry - Benji mentioned datadog. we have spans and token-level latency in Redwood Console; we can route telemetry to your DD with a small agent or via log-forwarder. priority is to get tracing mapped to your request IDs.
03:13 Benji Rao: what's the retention and PII handling? we have to ensure no raw prompts leak.
03:19 Olivia Chen: prompts are redacted by default in the staging export; we can share a redaction policy doc. for Private installs the redaction happens at the agent boundary and KMS keys remain customer-managed.
03:32 Benji Rao: good, please share the SOC2 attestation and the KMS integration steps.
03:36 Olivia Chen: will do - I'll attach the security pack.
03:40 Priya Desai: quick infra question - Marcus, you mentioned kernel 5.15, but our nodes are on 5.10 in prod. why the bump?
03:46 Marcus Rivera: we pushed 5.15 to pick up certain netfilter fixes and improvements to XDP path that improved tail latency in other pilots. but that introduced the PMTU regression on a subset of topologies.
03:57 Tomás Alvarez: so we need to test both 5.10 and 5.15 behaviors in our setup. can you run the same bench on 5.10 images?
04:04 Marcus Rivera: yes we'll run parity bench. that's part of the action items.
04:08 Olivia Chen: on routing, we also want to validate our smart routing policies - priority route by region then cost then latency. For your workload you said multi-region failover is required within 150ms SLA?
04:20 Eve Marshall: yes and we need deterministic tails, not just average. if failover adds jitter we fail the SLA.
04:26 Marcus Rivera: understood. we'll include 95th and 99th percentile metrics in the bench.
04:31 Priya Desai: do you have a recommended packet capture plan to correlate drops with our middleboxes?
04:35 Marcus Rivera: yes - enable tcpdump on the gateway and capture mtu-size flows during the test window. we'll provide a pcap filter.
04:41 Tomás Alvarez: we'll run captures in prod mirror for a short period once we have schedule.
04:45 Olivia Chen: scheduling - how about a canary next Tuesday 2027-04-20 for a 2-hour window targeting 3% of traffic?
04:53 Eve Marshall: that could work but need security signoff. Benji?
04:56 Benji Rao: pending my review of the KMS and redaction doc, but likely yes.
05:00 Priya Desai: also need to ensure the peering ACLs are opened up for the canary subnets; I'll change those but will need to coordinate change window.
05:07 Olivia Chen: fine - action item for Priya to share peering config by Friday the 16th.
05:11 Marcus Rivera: on benchmarks - I'll run with synthetic load and also a small replay of production traces (anonymized). expect an initial report by 2027-04-21.
05:20 Priya Desai: can you include the 1k request burst test? we saw a burn pattern last week under that load.
05:24 Marcus Rivera: yep that's part of the matrix: steady-state qps, burst 1k, and tail-burn scenario.
05:30 Olivia Chen: let me call out one more thing - observability mapping. we need to align on request ID propagation. their request IDs are X-Req-Id and we should map into Redwood trace id. Benji, any concerns?
05:41 Benji Rao: only that we redact token-level content and ensure X-Req-Id doesn't leak PII. seems ok.
05:46 Olivia Chen: perfect. any other blockers?
05:49 Tomás Alvarez: one more - egress bandwidth shaping. our cloud provider enforces burst limits; when the canary fires some flows hit the banked limit and throttle. is there a way to shape requests to smooth bursts?
05:58 Marcus Rivera: we can implement client-side pacing in the agent, or do server-side rate smoothing; both are doable. client-side pacing avoids building queues on the gateway.
06:10 Priya Desai: client-side pacing sounds better. can Redwood ship a pacing patch?
06:14 Marcus Rivera: yes small patch to the agent we can deliver as part of the canary.
06:18 Eve Marshall: timeline wise that needs to be small - we can't wait weeks. what's realistic?
06:22 Marcus Rivera: a few days for a patch build and internal QA, so if we start tomorrow we can have a candidate by Monday.
06:29 Olivia Chen: that fits the schedule. ok re: docs and artifacts - I will upload the canary playbook, fallback thresholds, and the preload script. Marcus will add bench results and the pcap filter. Priya will drop peering configs. Benji will review security pack.
06:44 Priya Desai: noted. also to avoid too many back-and-forths, can we use a single shared spreadsheet for benchmark matrices?
06:50 Olivia Chen: yes we'll create a shared sheet in the folder.
06:54 Tomás Alvarez: small nit - can we have a rollback signal that is manual and also an automated health signal? we don't want false positives causing rollback without ops consent.
07:02 Marcus Rivera: yes dual-mode rollback: manual abort plus automated if error rate > X% for Y minutes. we'll propose thresholds in the playbook.
07:11 Eve Marshall: perfect.
07:13 Olivia Chen: any other questions?
07:15 Benji Rao: please include the list of cipher suites supported for TLS on the private agent — compliance needs that.
07:20 Olivia Chen: will include.
07:22 Priya Desai: timeline recap?
07:24 Olivia Chen: quick recap — Priya share configs by 2027-04-16, Olivia will send canary playbook by 2027-04-15, Marcus runs benches and shares results 2027-04-21, Benji reviews KMS and returns notes by 2027-04-20. Canary target window 2027-04-20 (2-hour slot) pending Benji signoff.
07:44 Eve Marshall: sounds good. last thing — any cost implications if the fallback persists?
07:49 Marcus Rivera: fallback to local variant will be slightly cheaper per-token due to shorter hop, but if cache miss rate is high it could increase overall cost; we'll include an estimated cost delta in the bench report.
07:58 Olivia Chen: okay thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the shared folder and emaiI the calendar invite update for the canary window.
08:07 Tomás Alvarez: thanks all.
08:09 Olivia Chen: thanks, meeting adjourned.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Marcus to attach preload script gist and pcap filters.
- Olivia to attach canary playbook and security pack.
- Priya to upload peering configs and middlebox list.
- Benji to validate KMS steps and SOC2 notes.
- Set canary window tentative 2027-04-20 for 2 hours at low-traffic period; security signoff required.
